title: Opening: early drummer years and bands, 1915 on
summary: Bill introduces himself, says Alphonse Picou advised him to switch to trombone, and lists the bands he drummed with from 1915.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Bill Matthews, you can start anytime you wish and tell us a little bit about your life, when you were born, where and so on.

Bill Matthews, as old man Bill Matthews speaking, one of the New Orleans original who has been playing jazz for over 40 years, is still going strong, 1959. Born of New Orleans original drummers, 1915 to 1919, it was Alphonse P. Q. Suggestions, you were a young man Billy, my boy, why don't you learn some other instrument. So I've taken P. Q. advice, my choice was trombone. But before I quit playing drums, I was playing with some of the New Orleans best jazz bands. 1915, Buddy Petit, one of New Orleans jazz trumpet players. King Dooson, trombonist, former of Buddy Bowling. Kid René, one of Louis Armstrong's jazz boys that come up together. Jack Carey, known as King of the World as Tiger Ray. And old man Joe Johnson, one of the best trumpet players we ever had in the city of New Orleans. So sweet and so mellow. And old Sammy Morgan come along. Sammy had the best go here. Sammy did wonderful with his orchestra. Well, old man Robichaud picked me up, John Robichaud. I joined John Robichaud as drummer. I played with him a while.
